latest.question: Deputy Joe Cooney asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine if he will commit to maintaining a fully funded Areas of Natural Constraint scheme under the next CAP, particularly given the importance of ANC payments to farmers on marginal land in counties such as Clare.
latest.reply:
The Areas of Natural Constraints (ANC) scheme provides payments to people farming land in designated areas that face significant hardships from factors such as remoteness, difficult topography, climatic problems, and poor soil conditions. These payments are a valuable source of income support for farmers recognising the challenges for those situated in areas of natural and other specific constraints. Without this support, farming in these areas may not be viable and this could lead to the abandonment of agricultural land. Applicants apply for the Areas of Natural Constraints (ANC) scheme online via agfood.ie when submitting their annual Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS).
The draft CAP regulations allow member states to implement an ANC scheme in the years beyond 2027. I have publicly committed to including ANC in next CAP Strategic Plan. These regulations and the multi annual financial framework are not yet finalised and therefore the funding details for future years (beyond 2027) are not available at this time.
The annual indicative financial allocation for the intervention is €250m, amounting to a total indicative financial allocation of €1,250m for the period 2023-2027 and support will continue to be delivered on the ANC land categories for that period.
The following has been paid to ANC applicants since 2023.

latest.question: Deputy Barry Heneghan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine whether his Department has examined the feasibility of introducing a national food security reserve to strengthen Ireland’s resilience to potential food supply disruptions, including extreme weather events and international crises; and the measures that are currently in place to safeguard essential food supplies.
latest.reply:
While Ireland is one of the most food secure countries in the world, recent geopolitical crises have challenged established assumptions on food security and focused our attention to potential vulnerabilities in food production and supply. We are seeing conflict disrupting production, supply chains and markets, impacting most on vulnerable groups.
The EU Single Market and Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) are the critical mechanisms for ensuring food security throughout the European Union and Ireland. The European Union communication ‘Safeguarding food security and reinforcing the resilience of food systems” sets out actions in the three areas of food security, stability, and sustainability. The matter of food reserves is kept under review via the European Food Security Crisis preparedness and response Mechanism (EFSCM), which was established in 2021 to monitor and respond to threats to EU food security and supply. My Department has been an active participant in the EFSCM since its establishment.
Food security and protecting global food systems and strengthening supply chain resilience is a key focus for Ireland during our Presidency of the Council of the European Union, and beyond.
The Agriculture and Fisheries Council, which I currently Chair under Ireland’s Presidency, continues to support the work of the EFSCM, to ensure that we have adequate preparation for and responses to potential and real threats to global food security. latest.question: Deputy Pádraig O'Sullivan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the number of the 1,000 staff in his Department who have been designated as authorised officers who can carry out animal welfare inspections that are actually assigned to welfare inspections; the number of inspections carried out in each of the last three years; and whether the resourcing matches the enforcement role.
latest.reply:
Animal Welfare is a key priority for my Department. Consequently, all veterinary and technical One Health One Welfare operational staff are authorised under the Animal Health and Welfare Act 2013.
Being appointed as an authorised officer under the Act enables my officials to carry out animal welfare inspections as required and take appropriate and proportionate enforcement action. My Department’s One Health One Welfare Operations teams working in Regional Veterinary Offices and Department approved meat plants, are currently resourced by 265 veterinary and 354 technical staff.
The total number of inspections carried out by my Department is available in the table below.
In addition to the above inspections, all animals presented for slaughter at Department approved meat plants undergo an Animal Welfare inspection as part of their ante-mortem inspection.
My Department operates a confidential animal welfare helpline through which members of the public can report incidents of animal cruelty or neglect for investigation. The dedicated email address and helpline in place for reporting suspected cases of animal welfare are:

latest.question: Deputy John Clendennen asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the measures his Department is taking to reduce the administrative and paperwork burden on farmers.
latest.reply:
Simplification is central to the competitiveness of the agri-food sector and I will continue to advocate for the principle of simplification to remain a priority for the CAP post-2027.
Ireland advocates for making EU policy simpler and more workable for farmers and for national authorities. At the AGRIFISH Council on 26 October, the Irish Presidency secured unanimous agreement on a Partial General Approach (PGA) on the post-2027 CAP regulation.
Farmers need rules that are clear, proportionate and capable of being implemented effectively on the ground. The rules associated with farm payments should be applied in a practical way that recognises the realities of farming life and enables efficient administration.
There has been a lot of progress in that regard.
The Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) application system has been designed to allow farmers and their agents submit an application in the minimum number of steps. The system not only caters for BISS but a multitude of other area-based schemes and so farmers are given the opportunity to clearly see the options that they are choosing. In the majority of cases the application is pre-populated with the claim data from the previous years to make the application as straightforward as possible.

latest.question: Deputy Edward Timmins asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the progress being made to reduce bovine TB in Wicklow.
latest.reply:
I am very aware of the emotional and financial challenges for Irish farmers, their families and rural communities of a bovine TB (bTB) breakdown.
In September 2025 I launched the ‘Bovine TB Action Plan: Addressing Bovine TB in Ireland’ which includes 5 measures and 30 actions underpinned by scientific research, evidence and veterinary expertise. The aim of the Action Plan is to reset the TB programme by putting in place measures necessary to tackle the current disease situation.
There is a high incidence of bovine TB in Wicklow. As at 15 November 2026 over a 12 month period the national herd incidence was 5.56%, compared with 11.98% in Wicklow East and 20.49% in Wicklow West. The number of herds restricted nationally over a 12 month period was 5,511 compared with 106 herds in Wicklow East and 92 herds in Wicklow West, and the number of reactors nationally was 38,237 compared with 1,226 reactors in Wicklow East and 1,359 reactors in Wicklow West.
The reasons for bTB in certain herds and areas are multi-factorial and require a range of measures to address the issue. Each bTB outbreak is investigated by a veterinary inspector to identify the source of infection. In the case of every outbreak involving three or more standard reactors, there is a veterinary visit to advise the herd owner on how to eliminate infection and the measures necessary to help reduce the risk of recurrence. Farmers are also advised of bio-security measures they can take to reduce risks on their farm.

Ireland’s €258 million Seafood Development Programme 2021-2027, which is co-funded by the Government and the EU Commission under the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) is the primary source of funding for the Irish commercial seafood sector including the inshore sector.
My Department has reviewed all funding mechanisms currently available, either through the Seafood Development Programme itself or through other State Aid routes, to ascertain if there was a possibility to introduce a financial stabilisation scheme for inshore fishermen.

These rules also provide for added interest to be applied.

latest.question: Deputy Richard Boyd Barrett asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine to prioritise rural human rights, land justice, and the protection of Palestinian farmers by supporting the renewal of the UNDROP mandate (details supplied).
latest.reply:
The specific issue of supporting the UNDROP Declaration – the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Peasants and Other People Working in Rural Areas – is a matter for the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade. However, my Department has responsibility for some of the elements of Ireland’s international development programme and works closely with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade in this regard.
Specifically, my Department leads on Ireland’s engagement with the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization – a specialised UN agency leading global efforts to defeat hunger, improve nutrition, and ensure food security - and the United Nations World Food Programme, the UN’s frontline humanitarian agency.
In 2025, international development assistance funding to the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation comprised €4.34 million, including assessed contributions to FAO of €2.02 million and €2.31 million in discretionary funding for targeted projects and programmes.
This includes funding FAO’s project on the ‘The Right to Food in conflict-affected and protracted crisis contexts’. The scope of this project, which runs from April 2026 to March 2027, has particular relevance for Palestine, Ukraine, Myanmar, Colombia, Chad and Uganda. latest.question: Deputy Naoise Ó Muirí asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the progress being made by his Department in supporting farmers to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and achieve Ireland’s agricultural climate targets.
latest.reply:
The agriculture sector is committed to reducing its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 25% by 2030 in line with the 2021 Climate Act.
2025 was the fourth consecutive year of emission reductions from the sector and this reflects the efforts that farmers are putting in on the ground. Emissions for the sector were 4.7% lower in 2025 than in the Climate Act base year of 2018.
My Department is assisting farmers with their transition to more sustainable practices while also supporting family farm incomes with a budget of €9.8 billion under Ireland’s Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plan.
In practical terms, the types of actions that the Irish agriculture sector is undertaking include reducing the amount of chemical Nitrogen used, switching to low emission fertilisers and breeding the low emission animals of the future, together with voluntary diversification options.
Progress continues to be made, for example, the volume of chemical Nitrogen purchased by Irish farmers in 2025 was 15% lower than in the Climate Act base year of 2018.
Progress has also been made on the use of abatement technologies, for example, Low Emission Slurry Spreading is a key climate mitigation measure being implemented by our farmers that delivers on both climate and air quality emissions. Over 70% of Ireland’s slurry from livestock is now applied using this technology. latest.question: Deputy Peter Roche asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the measures his Department is taking to support generational renewal in farming, address barriers to farm succession, improve access to land and finance for young farmers and new entrants; and to encourage the timely transfer of family farms to the next generation, particularly in County Galway and the West of Ireland.
latest.reply:
The challenge of generational renewal in farming is widely recognised at both national and EU level and it is a priority of mine to ensure that farming is an attractive option for the next generation, including in the West of Ireland. Ensuring that younger generations can enter farming, invest in their businesses and build sustainable livelihoods is essential for the long-term competitiveness, resilience and sustainability of Irish agriculture.
Ireland’s CAP Strategic Plan 2023-2027 provides substantial resources to achieving generational renewal and measures include the Complementary Income Support for Young Farmers (CIS-YF); the National Reserve Scheme, which prioritises young farmers; and a higher grant rate of 60% for qualified young farmers under the TAMS capital investment measure. A Collaborative Farming Grant Scheme provides financial support to encourage farmers to form partnerships with young, trained farmers and the Succession Planning Advice Grant provides financial support towards the costs incurred for independent legal and financial advice for older farmers about succession planning.
Nationally, there are strong taxation measures to facilitate succession and assist land mobility. For succession, Agricultural Relief is the key measure, along with 100% Stamp Duty Relief and Consanguinity Stamp Duty Relief. Long-term leasing income tax relief supports access to land for young farmers and provides a route to retirement for older farmers.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.reply:

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.

Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. Mayo.
